findings.rule: c6 (20 per user per TailorMyResume day); claims.ts markUsed contract keyed by (userId, day, kind, key)
findings.trigger: An import claimed at 18:29:59.5Z (IST day D) whose fetch finishes at 18:30:03Z: claimAllowance (:686) writes PENDING on day D, but markUsed gets a second dependencies.now() and computes day D+1, so the upsert does not conflict and inserts a new USED row on D+1. The user gets 19 imports on D+1 and a stray PENDING row on D. analyses.ts:154/212 capture now once and tailoring.ts:227 passes row.createdAt for this reason.
findings.title: markUsed takes a fresh now(), so an import that crosses IST midnight is charged to the next day
findings.proof: Route test with now() returning 2026-10-11T18:29:59.900Z for the claim and 18:30:00.100Z after the fetch: expect one USED row on day D and none on D+1; at head the D+1 row exists. Fix: const now = dependencies.now() once, used for claimAllowance and markUsed.

findings.rule: Scale/availability: the PR's concurrency bound does not account for the shared libuv threadpool or per-user fairness
findings.trigger: One account points a domain at a name server that never answers and sends 4 concurrent imports (perUserPerMinute defaults to 60, src/apps.ts:94; busy 429s at :667 cost no allowance). dns.lookup runs getaddrinfo on the libuv threadpool (default 4 threads; Dockerfile sets no UV_THREADPOOL_SIZE). abortable (:191) frees the import slot at 8 s but cannot cancel the lookup, so all 4 threads stay busy until the stub resolver times out. Meanwhile the global cap of 4 (:626) answers 429 to every other user's import, and other threadpool work stalls, including pg Pool reconnect lookups (src/core/db/service.ts:2) and outbound fetches. Repeatable for 20 imports per account per day.
findings.title: Slow-DNS imports from one account fill the global import cap and the shared libuv threadpool
findings.proof: Cap starvation is testable now: inject a resolve port that never settles, start 4 imports as user A, then a 5th import by user B answers 429 RATE_LIMITED. The threadpool stall needs the real default port: with resolv.conf pointing at a local UDP listener that never replies, 4 pending defaultPorts.resolve calls delay an unrelated dns.lookup in the same process until the stub resolver times out. Fix sketch: resolve with dns.promises.Resolver (c-ares resolve4/resolve6 with a timeout and cancel() on abort, off the threadpool), and allow 1 running import per user.
